_comment: Standard mathematical notation. Entries rank below anything the paper itself says. Keys are canonical TeX (see render/mathunits.normalize) or a single Unicode character for operators recovered from MathJax.

\\mathbb{N}.name: the natural numbers
\\mathbb{N}.meaning: The natural numbers (whether 0 is included depends on the author).

\\mathbb{F}.name: a field
\\mathbb{F}.meaning: A field, often a finite field or a field of coefficients.

\\mathbb{Z}^{n}.name: integer lattice
\\mathbb{Z}^{n}.meaning: The lattice of integer vectors of length $n$; often used as a grading group (multidegrees).

\\mathbb{N}^{n}.name: non-negative integer vectors
\\mathbb{N}^{n}.meaning: Vectors of length $n$ with non-negative integer entries; often the grading group of a polynomial ring.

\\mathbb{R}^{\\operatorname{op}}.name: reals with reversed order
\\mathbb{R}^{\\operatorname{op}}.meaning: The poset of real numbers with the opposite order: $s \le t$ in $\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{op}}$ means $t \le s$ in $\mathbb{R}$. Persistence modules indexed by it have structure maps running from larger to smaller parameters.

\\mathfrak{m}.name: maximal ideal
\\mathfrak{m}.meaning: A maximal ideal; in a polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ usually the homogeneous maximal ideal $(x_1,\dots,x_n)$.

\\varepsilon.name: epsilon
\\varepsilon.meaning: Usually a small positive real number, or an interleaving/approximation parameter.

\\epsilon.name: epsilon
\\epsilon.meaning: Usually a small positive real number.

\\delta.name: delta
\\delta.meaning: Usually a small positive real number or a tolerance parameter.

\\partial.name: boundary / partial derivative
\\partial.meaning: The boundary operator (in homology) or a partial derivative (in analysis).

\\varnothing.name: empty set
\\varnothing.meaning: The empty set (also the empty face of a simplicial complex).

\\ell.name: ell
\\ell.meaning: An integer index or a length.

\\operatorname{Hom}.name: Hom
\\operatorname{Hom}.meaning: The set (or module) of homomorphisms between two objects.

\\operatorname{Ext}.name: Ext
\\operatorname{Ext}.meaning: The Ext functor: the right derived functors of $\operatorname{Hom}$.

\\operatorname{Tor}.name: Tor
\\operatorname{Tor}.meaning: The Tor functor: the left derived functors of the tensor product.

\\operatorname{Spec}.name: spectrum
\\operatorname{Spec}.meaning: The prime spectrum of a ring: the set of its prime ideals, with the Zariski topology.

\\operatorname{supp}.name: support
\\operatorname{supp}.meaning: The support of a module, vector, or function.

\\operatorname{coker}.name: cokernel
\\operatorname{coker}.meaning: The cokernel of a map: its codomain modulo its image.

\\operatorname{rank}.name: rank
\\operatorname{rank}.meaning: The rank of a linear map or module.

\\dim.name: dimension
\\dim.meaning: Dimension (of a vector space, module, or complex).

\\deg.name: degree
\\deg.meaning: The degree of a polynomial, monomial, or homogeneous element.

\\operatorname{lk}.name: link
\\operatorname{lk}.meaning: The link of a face $\sigma$ in a simplicial complex $\Delta$: all faces $\tau$ disjoint from $\sigma$ with $\tau \cup \sigma \in \Delta$.

\\operatorname{link}.name: link
\\operatorname{link}.meaning: The link of a face in a simplicial complex.

\\operatorname{del}.name: deletion
\\operatorname{del}.meaning: The deletion of a face $\sigma$ from a simplicial complex: all faces not containing (or disjoint from) $\sigma$.

\\operatorname{star}.name: star
\\operatorname{star}.meaning: The (closed) star of a face: all faces whose union with it is still a face.

\\operatorname{Dgm}.name: persistence diagram
\\operatorname{Dgm}.meaning: The persistence diagram of a persistence module or filtration.

\\operatorname{Vec}.name: vector spaces
\\operatorname{Vec}.meaning: The category of vector spaces (often finite-dimensional) over a fixed field.

\\mathbf{Vec}.name: vector spaces
\\mathbf{Vec}.meaning: The category of vector spaces (often finite-dimensional) over a fixed field.

\\operatorname{vect}.name: vector spaces
\\operatorname{vect}.meaning: The category of finite-dimensional vector spaces.

\\operatorname{Ann}.name: annihilator
\\operatorname{Ann}.meaning: The annihilator ideal of a module or element.

\\operatorname{Ass}.name: associated primes
\\operatorname{Ass}.meaning: The set of associated prime ideals of a module.

\\operatorname{depth}.name: depth
\\operatorname{depth}.meaning: The depth of a module: the length of a maximal regular sequence.

\\operatorname{ht}.name: height
\\operatorname{ht}.meaning: The height of a prime ideal.

\\varinjlim.name: direct limit
\\varinjlim.meaning: A direct limit (colimit over a directed system).

\\varprojlim.name: inverse limit
\\varprojlim.meaning: An inverse limit (limit over a directed system).

\\widetilde{H}.name: reduced homology
\\widetilde{H}.meaning: Reduced (co)homology: the ordinary theory with the contribution of a point removed, so $\widetilde{H}_{-1}(\varnothing)$ is one-dimensional.

\\Gamma_{\\mathfrak{m}}.name: torsion functor
\\Gamma_{\\mathfrak{m}}.meaning: The $\mathfrak{m}$-torsion functor: sends a module to the submodule of elements killed by a power of $\mathfrak{m}$.

d_{B}.name: bottleneck distance
d_{B}.meaning: The bottleneck distance between persistence diagrams (or barcodes).

d_{I}.name: interleaving distance
d_{I}.meaning: The interleaving distance between persistence modules.

d_{W}.name: Wasserstein distance
d_{W}.meaning: A Wasserstein distance between persistence diagrams.

\\beta_{i}.name: Betti number
\\beta_{i}.meaning: A Betti number: the rank of a homology group, or (graded) the rank of a term in a minimal free resolution.

\\beta_{i,j}.name: graded Betti number
\\beta_{i,j}.meaning: The graded Betti number $\beta_{i,j}$: the number of degree-$j$ generators in the $i$-th step of a minimal graded free resolution.

\\mu.name: mu
\\mu.meaning: Often a Bass number, a measure, or a Möbius function.

\\sigma.name: sigma
\\sigma.meaning: Often a face (simplex) of a simplicial complex, or a permutation.

\\tau.name: tau
\\tau.meaning: Often a face (simplex) of a simplicial complex.

H_{\\mathfrak{*}}^{*}.name: local cohomology
H_{\\mathfrak{*}}^{*}.meaning: Local cohomology with support in the ideal in the subscript: the right derived functors of the torsion functor $\Gamma_{\mathfrak a}(-)$, the submodule of elements killed by a power of $\mathfrak a$. The superscript is the cohomological degree.

H_{\\mathfrak{*}}^{\\bullet}.name: local cohomology
H_{\\mathfrak{*}}^{\\bullet}.meaning: Local cohomology (all degrees at once) with support in the ideal in the subscript.

H_{*}.name: homology
H_{*}.meaning: Homology in the degree given by the subscript.

H^{*}.name: cohomology
H^{*}.meaning: Cohomology in the degree given by the superscript.

\\widetilde{H}_{*}.name: reduced homology
\\widetilde{H}_{*}.meaning: Reduced homology in the degree given by the subscript; $\widetilde{H}_{-1}(\varnothing)$ is one-dimensional.

\\widetilde{H}^{*}.name: reduced cohomology
\\widetilde{H}^{*}.meaning: Reduced cohomology in the degree given by the superscript.

\\beta_{*}.name: Betti number
\\beta_{*}.meaning: A (graded) Betti number: the rank of a homology group, or the number of generators in a step of a minimal free resolution.

\\mu_{*}.name: Bass number
\\mu_{*}.meaning: Often a Bass number $\mu_i(\mathfrak p, M) = \dim_{k(\mathfrak p)} \operatorname{Ext}^i(k(\mathfrak p), M_{\mathfrak p})$: the multiplicity of the indecomposable injective $E(R/\mathfrak p)$ in the $i$-th term of a minimal injective resolution.

\\Gamma_{*}.name: torsion functor
\\Gamma_{*}.meaning: The torsion functor with respect to the ideal in the subscript: the elements killed by a power of that ideal.

M_{*}.name: graded piece / localization
M_{*}.meaning: For a graded module, the piece in the degree given by the subscript; for a ring element in the subscript, the localization at that element.

\\check{C}^{\\bullet}.name: Čech complex
\\check{C}^{\\bullet}.meaning: The Čech complex, whose cohomology computes local cohomology.

\\mathbf{e}_{*}.name: standard basis vector
\\mathbf{e}_{*}.meaning: The standard basis vector with a single 1 in the position given by the subscript.

x^{*}.name: monomial
x^{*}.meaning: A monomial $x^a = x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}$ with exponent vector $a$.

\\Delta_{*}.name: induced subcomplex / filtration step
\\Delta_{*}.meaning: Often the subcomplex of $\Delta$ induced on the vertex subset in the subscript, or a step of a filtration.

\\bullet.name: placeholder
\\bullet.meaning: A placeholder: $H^\bullet$ means the whole graded object (all degrees at once), and $F(-)$ or $F(\bullet)$ marks the slot of an argument.

\\ast.name: placeholder / dual
\\ast.meaning: A placeholder for an index or argument, or a dual / adjoint marker.

\\star.name: star
\\star.meaning: A distinguished element, a join operation, or a placeholder.

⨁.name: direct sum
⨁.meaning: Direct sum over an index set.

⨂.name: tensor product
⨂.meaning: Tensor product over an index set.

→.name: arrow
→.meaning: A map or morphism from the left object to the right one.

↦.name: maps to
↦.meaning: The element on the left is sent to the element on the right.

≤.name: less than or equal
≤.meaning: Less than or equal to (or the order relation of a poset).

⊂.name: subset
⊂.meaning: Is a subset of (authors differ on whether equality is allowed).

∖.name: set difference
∖.meaning: Set difference: elements of the left set not in the right set.

∘.name: composition
∘.meaning: Composition of maps (right map applied first).

≡.name: congruent
≡.meaning: Is congruent or identically equal to.

≔.name: defined as
≔.meaning: The left side is defined to be the right side.

∗.name: star
∗.meaning: A distinguished variant, dual, or convolution.

∧.name: wedge
∧.meaning: Meet, exterior product, or logical and.

∣.name: divides / such that
∣.meaning: Divides, or 'such that' in set-builder notation.

|.name: bar
|.meaning: Absolute value, cardinality, restriction, or 'such that'.

⟨.name: angle bracket
⟨.meaning: Inner product, generated ideal or subgroup, or pairing.

≺.name: precedes
≺.meaning: Strictly precedes in a partial order.

≼.name: precedes or equals
≼.meaning: Precedes or equals in a partial order.
